memory_candidates.content: Opening a negated Mathlib class hypothesis (not Archimedean, not IsSuccArchimedean, not DenselyOrdered) cannot be done by structure projection: use by_contra, then `push Not` (not the deprecated push_neg), then rebuild the class with the anonymous constructor from the negated goal. Worked example: from `IsLeast {z | 0 < z} u` and `not Archimedean D`, `exists x, forall n : Nat, n (nsmul) u < x` closes in five lines via nsmul_le_nsmul_right.

In this tree, a paper proposition of the form 'not valid over temporal order D' is rendered as `not (forall F : FrameOver D, F.toTaskFrame.ValidOn phi)` (the idiom validOn_df_iff_isDiscrete uses), and the bare Discrete class of record is the set `{F | F.IsRegular and F.IsDiscrete}` that galoisClosed_isDiscrete is stated over -- not FrameClass.ZTime, whose Sat is the strictly stronger IsZTime. A frame can be regular and IsDiscrete yet not IsZTime, which is exactly the gap every non-Archimedean discrete countermodel lives in.

Verifying a planned Lean deliverable with lean_run_code probes during the RESEARCH phase (full theorem bodies against real project imports, not isolated tactic attempts) turns implementation into transcription and surfaces every tactic-name and argument-order surprise before any file is edited. Cost here: five probes, three of which needed one or two iterations.
